answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a stake locked in a shared orchard of reputation: new agents start at the edge, like a young vine that must earn trust through verified work before accessing high-value jobs. A fake identity cannot shortcut this because every credential rests on a slow, verifiable history — a glacier of accumulated attestations — so creating thousands of fakes means paying the stake and waiting out the same delay for each, making the attack cost scale linearly while its payoff stays flat.
